Lightning never strikes the same place twice. Except, it does.
Guess how many times a year one building in New York gets hit. Comment a number.

text: The Empire State Building: about twenty three times a year.

Lightning loves tall, pointy, lonely things. Same spot, again and again.
And a blue sky doesn't mean you're safe.
A bolt from the blue can strike ten to fifteen miles from the storm.

text: If you can hear thunder, it's close enough to reach you.

Safe spots? A real building, or a car with a hard roof. Not a tree.
